name: PT Widodo Makmur Perkasa Tbk

frontmatter.title: WMPP: a protein recovery the holding structure does not pass on
frontmatter.summary: Widodo Makmur Perkasa is a holding company for cattle, feed, poultry and meat-processing businesses whose shares cost the market far more than the parent's own audited book. The recovery is real and the free-meals programme is a genuine demand driver, but nothing upstreams cash to the parent and the equity carries a deficit in retained earnings. Marked on the house conglomerate method, the parts are worth well below the price. SELL.
thesis: A holding company is worth its parts less what stands between them and the shareholder, and here that arithmetic lands well below the market: the parent's carrying value of its stakes less the corporate layer's net obligations leaves the parent's own audited equity, computed from the parent-entity statements — and the market pays more than that, for a group whose only route to cash for the minority — the upstream — has never run.

The operating turnaround is real and we do not discount it: sales grew 76.6% in the last audited year and 11.0% is our base case on the witnessed current-year rate. It is simply not big enough to close the gap to the price.

The discount is not a hope of narrowing: twenty to forty per cent is the house base rate for this structure, no cash has ever been upstreamed, and the parent cannot pay a dividend because its retained earnings are a deficit.

Most of the current year's reported profit is a restructuring gross-up, not trading: other income of 1,440 IDR bn sat against other expenses of a similar size while gross profit was a rounding error. We do not carry a one-off into the forecast.
The risk to this call is a dated, cash-upstreaming event at the parent — a subsidiary distribution, a stake sale, a parent-level capital return — none of which is on the register today.

catalysts.event: WMPP leaves the exchange's special-monitoring (full call auction) board, in the same measure that cuts the exchange's minimum share price to a single rupiah — the trading regime is normalised
The exchange's delisting of eighteen issuers takes effect; WMPP and its listed poultry subsidiary are not among them

blocks.text: **We initiate on WMPP with a SELL and a target of Rp12 against a market price of Rp25, a total return of -53.2%.** The method is the one the house card prescribes for a conglomerate and the industry config weights at 80% of the blend: value the parts, subtract what stands between the parts and the shareholder, then charge the holding-company discount the base rate says persists [S0]. On this name that exercise is unusually well sourced, because the LK publishes a parent-entity balance sheet alongside the consolidated one — the very statement the sum-of-the-parts needs and which most IDX registers do not carry [S3]. The parent's audited carrying value of its operating businesses is 1,227 IDR bn and its total liabilities are 1,632 IDR bn; netting the parent's other assets against those liabilities gives the corporate layer's net obligations, and the bridge closes to the parent's audited equity of 421 IDR bn [S3]. That closure is a computation, not a corroboration — it is an accounting identity, and the valuation section says so — but it means the two halves of the sum of the parts are sourced numbers rather than estimates [S3].

**What the market is paying for.** The shares cost Rp25 each, a market capitalisation of 735,475,000,000.0, on equity attributable to the parent of 254.7 at the last audited balance sheet [S0, S3]. Stated against each book in turn, because the direction differs: it is a large multiple of the group's own consolidated book of 254.7, a smaller one of the parent-entity's own audited equity of 421 IDR bn, and still below the parent's carrying value of the stakes themselves, 1,227 IDR bn, which is the mark the parts are struck against [S3, F6, F8]. The company lost -212.3 to its shareholders in the last audited year [S0, S3] and its consolidated net debt stood at 3,055.0, which is 750.6 times the restated EBITDA of 4.1 [S0, S3]. A price that rich needs either a recovery that reaches the parent's shareholders as cash, or a parts value we cannot see.

**The variant view is about where value sits, not about whether the business is recovering.** The recovery is on the record and we take it: revenue grew 76.6% in the last audited year [S0, S3], the first quarter of the current year printed sales of 288 IDR bn against 204 IDR bn a year earlier [S4], and the free-nutritious-meals programme is a real, budgeted demand shock that the company's own annual report sizes at 191,210 tonnes of beef alone, inside a national beef-consumption forecast of 964,166 tonnes [S2]. Our disagreement is with the *destination* of that recovery. It sits in operating subsidiaries that do not distribute, behind a parent whose own cash is 0.2 IDR bn and whose retained earnings are a deficit [S3]: the recovery improves the consolidated accounts without ever reaching the shareholder of the listed parent as cash.

**What moves the value.** First, the discount. Second, the carrying value of the parts: we mark them at the parent's own audited book, which is roughly five times what the consolidated accounts say the same net assets are worth to the parent's shareholders [S3] — so the mark we use is the generous one, and a stricter reading lowers the answer rather than raising it. Third, any dated action that actually upstreams cash, which is the single item that would justify a narrower discount [S0]. Two honest limits are stated in the valuation section rather than buried: the parent's long-term related-party receivables are carried at face because the register carries no impairment assessment of them, and the rights issue under way at the separately listed poultry subsidiary — up to 6,100,000,000 new shares — is carried only as a dilution risk rather than valued, because the register does not state its subscription terms and the parent's own cash of IDR0.2bn cannot fund its share [S3, S8, S11, F7, F51].

PT Widodo Makmur Perkasa describes itself in its own accounts as a holding company — "Kegiatan usaha Perusahaan adalah Perusahaan holding serta perdagangan besar dan peternakan sapi" — and lists its business scope as general trading, cattle, poultry, meat, soybean and rice, engineering consultancy, mining and energy, and construction work [S3]. What has actually been running, on the company's own list, is wholesale trade and cattle breeding, slaughterhouses, wholesale trade of meat and processed meat, chicken farming, livestock-feed trading, wholesale trade of agricultural food and beverage products, and construction, carried on both directly and through subsidiaries [S3]. The chairman and controlling shareholder is Mr Tumiyana, who is also president director; the last audited year closed with 499 people employees on the payroll [S3, F41].

The company reports six operating segments, and their revenue shares are worth stating because they explain the margin structure. In the last audited year the carcass and meat-processing business was the largest by a wide margin at 643 IDR bn of sales, followed by construction at 221 IDR bn, poultry at 118 IDR bn, animal feed at 78.9 IDR bn, trading and other at 19.5 IDR bn, and cattle farming at 7.6 IDR bn [S3]. Meat trading and construction together are roughly four fifths of the top line. That mix — trading and building against a much smaller farming and processing base — is why group gross margin is thin and stays thin, and it is why a revenue recovery does not translate mechanically into profit [S3].

The poultry business is operated through a subsidiary that is itself listed: PT Widodo Makmur Unggas Tbk (WMUU), in which the group holds 76.6% of the equity, runs the integrated chicken chain from feed mill through day-old chicks to a slaughterhouse at Giritontro in Wonogiri that the company says can process up to 12,000 birds per hour [S2, F42, F50]. It is the group's only separately quoted asset, and its shares traded at Rp36 in the third week of October 2026 [S9, F49]. That listed arm is also where the group's main expansion is happening, and where a rights issue was being arranged in the current year — up to 6,100,000,000 of new shares, a subscription the parent cannot fund from its own cash of IDR0.2bn and which therefore dilutes the parent's interest unless a third party funds it [S8, S11, F7, F51]. The cattle side runs at Cianjur in West Java and through a feedlot operation, with the company targeting a minimum daily weight gain per head and describing premium domestic beef-breeding as a strategic objective [S8].

Ownership is concentrated and the float is thin. Insider holdings are reported at 79.6 against a free float of 21.2 [S0], the issued capital is 588 IDR bn at a nominal par value [S3], and there is one controlling family interest at the top of the structure [S3, F41]. The company has never paid a dividend [S0].

The corporate history is not incidental to what a share is worth. The group took a foot-and-mouth disease outbreak on its cattle herd in 2022, spent the following years in a debt restructuring, and was put into a postponement of debt payment obligations by the commercial court in December 2024 before reaching a peace agreement with its creditors [S3, F38]. The consequences are still on the balance sheet: a dedicated line for the homologated debt, 15.6 IDR bn of it falling due within a year, and a long-term related-party payable of 194 IDR bn [S3, F23, F24]. The exchange suspended trading in the shares and placed them on the special-monitoring board, from which they were removed with effect from 28 September 2026 [S6, S7, F35].

Indonesian integrated protein businesses are usually described by where they sit on the chain from
feed to plate. The economics differ sharply along it: feed milling and day-old-chick production carry
brand and technical barriers and earn a spread, live-bird farming is a commodity with a disease and
feed-cost cycle, and slaughtering and meat trading is closer to a distribution business where volume
matters more than price. A holding company that owns several points on that chain describes itself as
integrated, but the consolidated margin is a blend of all of them and tends toward whichever part is
largest. Institutional catering, school-meal and defence procurement contracts can change the volume
picture quickly in this market, but they are awarded through tenders with fixed menus and price
ceilings, so they lift volume more reliably than they lift margin.

The demand backdrop the company itself cites is a step change in domestic protein consumption created by the government's free-nutritious-meals programme. The annual report states that national beef and buffalo consumption in the current year is projected to rise by around a tenth to 964,166 tonnes, with the meals programme assumed to absorb 191,210 tonnes of that [S2]. Whether or not that specific split proves right, the direction is a sourced fact about the market this company sells into, and the company has built its expansion plan on it: a stated revenue target of 2,100 IDR bn for the current year against 1,011.9 in the last one — a figure the reporting source labels a first-quarter number, though its own comparison base is the full prior year and a first quarter is impossible on the sales actually printed [S8, F29] — additional slaughterhouse capacity, a laying-hen population rising from 350,000 birds today to 1,000,000 birds by 2028, and feedlot expansion across West Java, Central Java, East Java and the new capital region [S8, F29, F33, F34].

That plan is where we part company with the company, and the parting is arithmetic rather than judgement. To reach the stated target, the second half of the current year would have to run at roughly two and a half times the second half of the last one, while the first quarter of the current year came in at 288 IDR bn against 204 IDR bn in the comparable quarter — a little over two fifths higher, which annualises to about the 11.0% we carry [S4, S8]. We have checked that rejection against the source that states the period unambiguously: the target's own comparison base is the last audited year's full revenue of 1,011.9, and a target of 2,100 IDR bn inside a single quarter is impossible when the group printed 288 IDR bn in the first quarter, so the figure is the annual plan and the reject-the-plan arithmetic stands [S4, S8, F3, F29, F30]. The programme may well be a multi-year volume driver; nothing in the register supports it doubling the group's top line inside one year.

Competitively the group is a follower, not a price setter, and the structure of its own segments says so. Its largest revenue line is meat trading and carcass supply [S3], where it competes against much larger integrated poultry producers and against importers; its construction arm is a contractor inside a crowded domestic market [S3]; its cattle operation is small relative to the national herd and has just been through a disease shock [S3, F38]. The two places where it has something that resembles a moat are the slaughter and processing assets — a licensed abattoir with the capacity the company cites, which is a permissioned asset that cannot simply be replicated [S2, F28] — and the feed and day-old-chick operation inside the listed poultry subsidiary, where technical capability matters [S2]. Both sit below the parent, in subsidiaries with their own minority shareholders, which is the central fact of this report.

The regulatory and policy backdrop cuts both ways for a name this size. The meals programme is a demand subsidy with a budget behind it, but it is also the single demand assumption our base case leans on, and the company's own stated target depends on that programme delivering far faster than the first quarter did [S2, S8, F26, F29]. Its conduct is not something this register lets us audit — there is no disclosed finding, charge or investigation we can cite, and we assert none — which is exactly why we carry the witnessed run-rate rather than the plan. The company also operates in a listing regime that has just changed around it: the exchange removed ninety-two issuers from the special-monitoring board and cut the exchange's minimum share price to Rp1.0 with effect from 28 September 2026, naming WMPP among the ninety-two [S7, F35, F36]. Cutting the old minimum price to a single rupiah removes a floor that had been supporting the price of exactly this kind of small-capitalisation name — a market-structure change that matters to a stock trading at Rp25 [S0, S7].

FX is a lesser exposure than it looks for the revenue line, since the company states its products are marketed domestically [S3], but it is a larger one for costs: animal feed is built on imported soybean meal and corn substitutes, and the house macro deck prices the rupiah at Rp18,350/USD to the dollar against a spot of Rp18,110/USD [S0]. Against that sits domestic demand growth the deck puts at 5.3 rate for the coming year [S0], which is the assumption the long-run end of our revenue path leans on.

The reported history is a company that nearly stopped. Revenue ran at 4,390.1 two years before the last audited one, collapsed to 907.2 and then 572.9, and recovered to 1,011.9 [S0, S3]. The recovery is genuine — 76.6% — but it is a recovery off a trough, and it brought the group back only to roughly a quarter of where it started. Gross margin went from a negative -16.6% to a barely positive 0.3% [S0, S3], and the reported net result attributable to the parent was -212.3 [S0, S3]. This is not a business that lost money because of a cyclical squeeze; it lost money at the level of the whole operation.

A definitional correction comes first, because it changes every margin in the model. The data pack's depreciation line is a fraction of the real charge: the IDX cash-flow statement is prepared on the direct method and carries no add-back, so the pack records 104.9 for the last audited year when the LK's own fixed-asset note shows 105 IDR bn, and 101.5 against 101 IDR bn for the year before [S0, S3, F1, F2]. We restate both years from the filing, and the engine rebuilds EBITDA from them. Two further lines are restated for the same reason: the pack reports operating expenses of a different order from the LK's own operating-expense line and a correspondingly different operating loss, because the data feed folds part of the other-income and other-expense block into the operating line [S3, F45, F46, F47, F48]. Restated, the last audited year's operating loss was -100.9 and its EBITDA was 4.1 — positive, but a rounding error on 1,011.9 of sales [S3].

Our forecast does not extrapolate the trough and does not take the plan. Revenue grows 11.0% in the current year, which is the first half's witnessed rate annualised — sales of 288 IDR bn in the first quarter against 204 IDR bn in the comparable quarter of the last year [S4, F30, F31] — and then tapers toward the house deck's long-run expansion assumption for Indonesia [S0]. Gross margin is held at 1.1%, the rate the current year has actually printed rather than the trough of the audited year [S4], and operating expense is held at the last audited year's own ratio of expense to revenue [S3]. On those settings EBITDA is 13.8 and the loss attributable to the parent is -281.3 [S0]: the group is still loss-making at the net line even with the recovery, because the restated depreciation charge of 116.5 and the finance cost on debt of 3,061.0 outrun an EBITDA margin of 1.2% [S0, S3].

**Earnings quality, through the house screen, line by line.** *Accruals*: on the group's reported figures the accruals screen is not the problem — cash from operations was a small positive in the last audited year against a loss, because the loss is dominated by non-cash depreciation, other-expense write-offs and finance cost rather than by accrual inflation of profit [S0, S3]. What the screen does show is that the reported *profit* in the current year is not earned: the first quarter booked other income of 1,440 IDR bn against other expenses of a comparable size, leaving a gross profit of a few billion rupiah and a positive pre-tax line [S4, F32]. We read that as a restructuring event — the peace agreement working through the accounts — and we carry none of it into the forecast. *Cash conversion*: operating cash flow covered only a fraction of the finance bill in the last audited year, with finance costs of 106.9 [S0, S3], and the group funds itself from restructured debt rather than from operations. *Board status*: this is the single largest improvement in the file. The shares spent a long period suspended and on the exchange's special-monitoring board and were removed from it with effect from 28 September 2026 [S6, S7, F35]; the issuer is not on the exchange's delisting list of eighteen names that takes effect in November 2026 [S6, F37]. *Related parties*: quantified and material at the parent, where the parent carries a long-term related-party receivable of IDR419.4bn — of which IDR176.0bn is due from the controlling shareholder's own vehicle, an interest-free and unsecured loan of May 2021 carried unchanged at face with no provision [S3, F52, F53] — against a long-term related-party payable of 194 IDR bn and a total liability stack of 1,632 IDR bn [S3, F10, F24]. A receivable from the controller's own vehicle, interest-free and unsecured, is the modal value-leak channel in this market (the related-party gravity channel of the earnings-quality card), and it sits inside the asset base that produces the parts value: the base case carries it at face because the register carries no impairment, and the bear case treats it as impaired. That is one reason we do not give the name the tight end of the discount band. *PSAK 16 check*: the group does revalue land, and a revaluation surplus sits in equity from the last audited year [S3]; the mark we use is the parent's carrying value of its investments rather than a book figure flattered by that surplus, so the check does not bite on the primary method, but a reader using the consolidated book cross-check should know the revaluation is in it [S3]. *Structure flags*: the restructuring itself, the homologated-debt line [S3, F23], the deficit in the parent's retained earnings [S3, F44], and a controlling shareholder who is also the president director [S3, F41]. On the card's classification rule these are optics-class — disclosed, explained in the accounts, and audited — rather than manipulation-class: nothing in the register alleges fabricated cash or fictitious revenue, and the auditor's going-concern framing sits alongside the directors' own going-concern assertion rather than replacing it [S3, F39]. We therefore do not route the name to the card's auto-pass; we charge it in the discount.

Working capital and capital spending are both quiet. Operating working capital was roughly two thirds of sales at the last balance sheet, and we hold that ratio flat [S3]. Capital spending of 6.6 in the last audited year was close to nil because the large poultry build is already on the balance sheet and is being finished — the LK states the work in progress is a little over half complete with completion targeted in late 2027 [S3]. The consequence is that the group's free cash flow is a financing story, not an operating one: on our settings the modelled firm-level free cash flow is -54.7 [S0], and the modelled balance sheet runs thinner each year because we refuse to invent a debt schedule for a company whose debt is fixed by a court homologation [S3, F23].

Capital allocation is stark and it is the heart of the equity story. Since the initial public offering the group has raised equity once, at the listing, and has returned nothing: no dividend has ever been declared and none can be, because the parent's unappropriated retained earnings are a deficit [S0, S3, F44]. Cash that the businesses generate is retained inside them or applied to the restructured debt, and the parent's own cash balance is 0.2 IDR bn [S3]. For a minority holder of the listed parent, that is the whole difference between owning a recovery and owning a claim on a recovery that never arrives.

The house card for conglomerates is the reason this name is modelled as it is. A holding company is worth its parts — listed stakes at market, unlisted businesses on their own terms — less the holdco layer, less a discount the base rate says persists [S0]. The industry config puts the sum of the parts at 80% of the blend, an earnings cross-check at 0% and a book cross-check at 20%, struck on the group's own multiple history [S0]. The cost of capital behind the cross-checks is the rupiah risk-free rate of 7.4%, the industry unlevered beta of 0.90 re-levered to a market debt-to-equity of 2.00 — which produces a levered beta of 2.30 and, with a mature-market equity risk premium of 4.2% and a country premium of 2.5%, a cost of equity of 21.2% and a weighted average cost of capital of 12.0% [S0]. The high gearing is a fact of this company, not a modelling choice: debt is 3,061.0 against equity attributable to the parent of 254.7 [S0, S3]. No discounted-cash-flow method is used at all, because the industry's method set for a conglomerate does not include one.

**The parts, and how they are marked.** One part can be marked at market, and we disclose it: the group's poultry business is a separately quoted company, PT Widodo Makmur Unggas Tbk, in which the parent holds 76.6% [S2, F42, F50], and its shares traded at Rp36 in the third week of October 2026 [S9, F49]. But the parent's investment line is a SINGLE audited figure — its carrying value of all its subsidiaries, 1,227 IDR bn — and the filing does not break out the carrying value of the poultry arm within it, so the arm's market level cannot be substituted for its book share of that line without double-counting [S3, F6]. What the register does carry, and almost no IDX filing does, is the parent entity's own balance sheet in the appendix, which states the parts line at 1,227 IDR bn [S3]. We therefore mark the whole line at the parent's own audited book, say so plainly, disclose the listed arm's market level beside it, and treat a re-rating of that arm — in either direction — as the parts' largest identifiable swing factor; we do not claim the book mark is a market mark, and no blanket multiple is applied, which the card forbids. The segment note gives revenue by part, which we use in the business section [S3, F11-F16], but its asset and liability columns are presented in a form the register cannot attribute reliably to each part [S3, F17, F18].

| Component | Mark | Basis | | --- | --- | --- | | Operating businesses held through the parent's investments in subsidiaries | parent-entity audited book | 1,227 IDR bn of investment in shares at the last audited year-end — a single line that includes the listed poultry arm [S3] | | Listed poultry arm (PT Widodo Makmur Unggas Tbk) | disclosed, not re-marked | parent holds 76.6% of the arm, quoted at Rp36 in October 2026; its carrying value is not broken out of the line above, so it is disclosed beside it rather than netted into it [S2, S9, F6, F49, F50] | | Corporate layer — the parent's whole liability stack less its non-stake assets | deduction | IDR1,632.1bn of parent total liabilities against the parent's non-stake assets (cash IDR0.2bn, related-party receivable IDR419.4bn, fixed assets IDR267.6bn and the deferred-tax and other balances at the centre), netting to the corporate layer's obligations [S3, F7, F10, F53, F54] | | Holding-company discount | deduction | the house base rate of twenty to forty per cent, charged at the level argued below [S0] | | Liquidity | deduction | the house schedule applies where three-month traded value is thin; the engine charges 10% [S0] |

The bridge is a computation, not an estimate — and not a corroboration either, which we say plainly. Because the parts line is itself a parent-entity asset, "parts less the corporate layer equals parent equity" is an accounting identity: 1,227 IDR bn of parts plus the parent's non-stake assets less its total liabilities of 1,632 IDR bn equals the parent's audited equity of 421 IDR bn by construction [S3, F6, F8, F10]. It proves the two halves reconcile to the accounts; it does not prove the parts are marked correctly. On this method the primary is therefore a parent-book net asset value, and before the holdco discount it is arithmetically the parent's own book value. The sum-of-the-parts method values the equity at Rp9 a share AFTER that discount [S0].

**Three things about that mark, stated plainly because all three make it generous.** First, the parent's carrying value of its stakes stands at roughly five times the consolidated net assets attributable to the parent, 254.7 [S3, F6, F19]: the losses have been recognised in the consolidated accounts but the parent has not written its investments down. Marking the parts at consolidated equity instead would produce a smaller number, not a larger one [S3, F19]. Second, the parent's long-term related-party receivable of IDR419.4bn is carried at face, and IDR176.0bn of it is an interest-free, unsecured loan to the controlling shareholder's own vehicle carried unchanged and unprovided [S3, F52, F53]; an impairment of it would lower the parts. Third, the listed poultry arm is the one part that CAN be marked independently, and we disclose its market level rather than net it [S9, F49]; a re-rating of that arm moves the parts in either direction, which is why it is named as the largest identifiable swing factor. All three mean that a reader who thinks the mark should be stricter should expect a *lower* parts value than ours, which is why the sensitivity grid matters and why the call survives the reweighting discussion below.

**The holdco layer, and what cannot be netted.** The card asks for holdco net debt; we net the parent's whole corporate layer, and we say why rather than rename it. The parent's IDR1,632.1bn of liabilities is overwhelmingly intra-group and related-party payables rather than bank debt — its long-term related-party other payables alone are IDR582.1bn — and its non-stake assets (cash of IDR0.2bn, the long-term related-party receivable of IDR419.4bn, fixed assets of IDR267.6bn and the deferred-tax and other balances at the centre) are netted in full [S3, F5, F7, F10, F53, F54]. Netting only debt-less-cash would leave the IDR582.1bn-scale related-party payables out of the bridge and flatter the answer, because the parent's obligations are payables to related parties, not borrowings it could refinance; so the layer is the whole net corporate obligation, not the card's narrower term, and the report calls it that throughout. The card also asks for holdco overhead capitalised at around ten times; that we cannot produce, because the parent's own operating expenses are disclosed as a single line that mixes corporate overhead with everything else [S3]. We flag it rather than estimate it, and note that on the card's own convention the missing item is worth a fraction of one per cent of the parts value — leaving it out does not flatter the target. The third output the card asks for, the upstream-coverage ratio, is zero in the most literal sense: the parent has received nothing, because nothing has been distributed, and it could not lawfully declare a distribution from a deficit of retained earnings [S0, S3, F44].

**The discount.** The base rate is that a holding-company discount of twenty to forty per cent persists indefinitely, and the card requires a named, dated catalyst that actually upstreams cash before a narrower discount can be underwritten [S0]. This name has no such catalyst on the register. It has never paid a dividend and cannot from a deficit of retained earnings [S0, S3, F44]; the parent's own cash is 0.2 IDR bn against a company-level liability stack of 1,632 IDR bn [S3]; there is no buyback, no tender and no announced stake sale [S7, S8]; and the only capital action in the file — the rights issue at the listed poultry subsidiary — raises money at that entity and dilutes the parent's interest in it rather than sending value up [S8]. Set against that are the two facts that argue for the tight end: the trading regime has been normalised, with the shares off the special-monitoring board since 28 September 2026 [S7, F35], and the operating recovery is real [S4]. We charge thirty-five per cent: off the middle because the cash-upstream channel has never run and cannot run from a deficit, short of the wide end because the listing status is now normal and the businesses are trading. The choice is not load-bearing — even at the tight end of the band the value stays below the price — and the sensitivity grid lets a reader take a different view [S0].

**Two charges, two different factors, stated because both price illiquidity.** The holdco discount prices the STRUCTURE — the agency of the centre and a cash-upstream channel that has never run — and is the base-rate band for any holding company [S0]. The house liquidity schedule prices the MARKET for this particular stock, and the engine applies it to any name whose traded value falls under the threshold, whatever its structure [S0]. A deep, liquid holdco would carry the first and not the second; a liquid non-holdco under the threshold would carry the second and not the first. We therefore charge both, disclose the compound effect, and note that the conclusion turns on neither: the parts sit below the price before any discount is applied, so a reader who drops one charge or the other still does not arrive at the price [S0].

**Why no dated catalyst is named for the gap to close.** The card requires a named, dated catalyst before a *narrower* discount can be underwritten. We are not underwriting a narrowing; the call is the opposite, and it rests on the ABSENCE of such an event — no dated action on this register upstreams cash, and the parent cannot distribute from a deficit of retained earnings [S0, S3, F44]. The dated items the file does carry are the trading-regime change of 28 September 2026 and the delisting confirmation of 10 November 2026 [S6, S7, F35, F37]; both are recorded. Because the SELL is a structural call on the mark and the upstream rather than a bet on a dated event, and because the price is thin and recently resumed, we would file it as lower-conviction on timing even though the direction is robust [S0, S6, S7].

**The cross-checks, and why one of them disagrees.** The earnings cross-check is unavailable, and that is itself evidence: the group's earnings are negative on our restated numbers, so a P/E cannot be struck and the engine drops the method [S0]. The direction of that absence matters — applying any plausible multiple to a loss is not a valuation, and the method's disappearance raises the weight the parts carry rather than lowering the answer. The book cross-check applies the group's own five-year average P/BV of 1.3 to the latest reported equity and produces Rp17 a share, 78.7% above the primary [S0]. We explain the divergence rather than ignore it, and the explanation is the frozen price. The shares traded at a fixed nominal level through a long suspension and only returned to trading in 2026 [S0, S6, S7], so the own-history P/BV sample is not a set of market observations of this business — it is a stale quotation divided by a book value that has since shrunk. The gap is therefore not a second opinion on the parts; it is a record of a price that was not being made.

**The price we measure the return against, held to the same standard.** We use the same quotation for the return that we call stale for the P/BV sample, and we state the tension rather than hide it: Rp25 is the last print on a name whose three-month traded value is 1,991,167,257.1 and which was suspended through the second half of 2024 and only returned to trading in March 2026 [S0, S6, S7]. It may not be a fully made price. The expected return is therefore struck against a thin, recently-resumed quotation, and the magnitude of -53.2% should be read with that caution. What does NOT depend on the print is the direction: the parts, carried at the parent's own audited book, sit below Rp25 before any discount is charged, so the sign of the call survives a stale quote even if its size does not [S0].

**How the target is built.** The parts method values the equity at Rp9 a share, the weighted blend of the methods is Rp11, and the twelve-month target of Rp12 is that blend grown one year at the cost of equity — the engine's house construction, applied to every name, not a forecast that the parent's book compounds at the required return [S0]. There is no dividend leg, because the company pays none, and the house liquidity charge of 10% is then taken [S0]. The target sits -53.2% below the price [S0].

The sensitivity grid is driven by the discount and the cost of capital, and that is the framework's honest limitation here rather than a hidden one: the primary method marks the parts at audited book, so a forward shock to revenue or margin moves the income statement without moving the target [S0]. A reader who wants the operating case to drive the answer needs the parts marked on their own earnings cards, which requires segment profit and capital-employed disclosure this register does not carry [S3]. What today's price implies is the reciprocal of that limitation: for the value to reach Rp25, the parts would have to be worth well above the parent's own audited carrying value of them, or the discount would have to be eliminated entirely — and the parts mark is already the generous one [S0, S3].

**Bear case** (25%): the first quarter's profit was a restructuring gross-up rather than trading [S4, F32]; the free-meals procurement is re-tendered or delayed, so the company's plan misses [S2, S8]; and the parts mark proves unsupportable — the controlling shareholder's interest-free receivable of IDR176.0bn is impaired, and the listed poultry arm's rights issue of up to 6,100,000,000 new shares dilutes the parent's 76.6% interest because the parent's own cash of IDR0.2bn cannot fund its share of the subscription [S3, S11, F7, F51, F52]. The engine's bear leg gives Rp10 a share and a target of Rp12 [S0]. **Base case** (55%): the recovery continues at the witnessed rate, the parts stay at the parent's audited book, and the discount stays where the evidence puts it — Rp11 a share, Rp13 target [S0]. **Bull case** (20%): a return of cash to the parent, a stake sale or a subsidiary action that crystallises a mark narrows the discount to the tight end of the band, with the meals programme's demand delivered into the group's slaughter and processing capacity [S2, F26, F28] and the laying-hen and feedlot plan arriving on schedule [S8] — Rp12 a share and Rp14 [S0].

**What the scenario layer can and cannot express, said rather than implied.** The bear narrative names a parts write-down; the model's parts are a sourced fact — the parent's audited carrying value of 1,227 IDR bn — and the scenario engine can only shock the drivers it holds as inputs (the discount and the revenue rate), not a book fact [S0]. Rather than leave the narrative promising a lever the model cannot pull, the bear expresses the downside through the lever it can — the discount widening toward the wide end of the band — and the parts-write-down arithmetic is stated in words in the valuation section above [S0, S3]. On the bull side the register offers no further *modelable* lever, and we say so: the poultry arm's carrying value is not broken out of the single investment line, so it cannot be re-marked without double-counting, and the land revaluation surplus is already inside book equity [S3, F6]. That cap is why the bull probability sits below the bear's rather than at an even split [S0]. Even the bull leg does not reach Rp25; the asymmetry is structural, not engine-imposed — a bull can narrow a discount that already sits inside a band, but it cannot conjure an upstream no source shows, and it cannot raise a book mark the register does not let us re-strike.

Five risks carry weight. **Governance and control (high likelihood, high impact)**: one family interest controls the company and the same person is chairman and president director [S3, F41], insider holdings are reported at 79.6 against a float of 21.2 [S0], and the parent's balance sheet is dominated by related-party balances in both directions [S3] — minority holders have no practical influence over whether cash is ever distributed. **Balance sheet and liquidity (high likelihood, high impact)**: the group's debt is fixed by a court-homologated peace agreement, 15.6 IDR bn of it falls due within a year, and the parent's own cash is 0.2 IDR bn [S3, F7, F23]; a missed instalment would put a solvency question back on the table. **Demand concentration (medium likelihood, high impact)**: the expansion plan leans on a single government programme whose procurement and conduct are politically exposed, and the company's own stated target depends on that programme delivering far faster than the first half did [S2, S8]. **Margin (high likelihood, medium impact)**: the largest revenue lines are low-margin trading and construction [S3], so a small move in feed cost or live-bird price can wipe out a gross margin that is barely above zero 1.1% [S0]. **Market structure (medium likelihood, medium impact)**: the exchange has just removed the minimum share price, which for a stock at Rp25 removes a support that had nothing to do with the business [S0, S7, F36]. A sixth sits behind all of them — liquidity. Three-month traded value is 1,991,167,257.1 [S0], thin enough that the house schedule charges a discount of 10%, and thin enough that the position could not be exited quickly.

Signposts that would change the view: any dated action that actually upstreams cash to the parent — a subsidiary dividend, a parent-level distribution, a stake sale, a buyback — would justify a narrower discount and is the one thing that changes this call [S0, S3]; a missed homologation instalment or an auditor's qualification on the current-year accounts would widen it [S3, F23]; and segment disclosure of profit and capital employed would let us mark the parts on their own cards instead of at the parent's book, in either direction [S3].

Ownership is concentrated in a single controlling interest, with insider holdings reported at 79.6 and a free float of 21.2 [S0, S3]. The controlling shareholder is also the president director [S3, F41], so the same person sets strategy and represents the controlling block on the board; minority holders have no practical influence over board composition and none at all over the group's decision to reinvest rather than distribute [S3]. The board carries two commissioners, one of them independent, and an audit committee, and the filing's governance section shows the committee meeting through the year [S3]. The company's own disclosures place it in a normal governance posture for a small IDX issuer, and nothing in the register alleges fabrication — the flags here are structural and disclosed rather than concealed [S3].

Related-party dealings are the governance fact that matters most, and they are disclosed. At the parent level the parent carries a long-term related-party receivable of IDR419.4bn — IDR176.0bn of it due from the controlling shareholder's own vehicle, interest-free, unsecured and unprovided [S3, F52, F53] — against a long-term related-party payable of 194 IDR bn and total liabilities of 1,632 IDR bn [S3, F10, F24]. A loan from the group to the controller's own vehicle, on no interest and no security, is the modal value-destruction channel in this market (the related-party gravity channel of the earnings-quality card), and it is the clearest single illustration of who decides how value moves inside this structure. The company has never paid a dividend and cannot lawfully declare one, because the parent's unappropriated retained earnings are a deficit [S0, S3, F44]; that is a governance fact as much as a financial one, because minority holders' only route to the cash the businesses generate is closed by the account the businesses themselves produced.

The listed-status file has improved materially and is the strongest part of the story. The shares were suspended by the exchange and placed on the special-monitoring board, from which WMPP was removed with effect from 28 September 2026 in the same measure that cut the exchange's minimum share price to Rp1.0 [S7, F35, F36]; the issuer is not among the eighteen names the exchange will delist in November 2026 [S6, F37]. The company states the going-concern basis of accounting continues to apply and its directors expect adequate resources for the foreseeable future [S3, F39] — the standard assertion, in a company whose own note records a loss of -234.9 for the last audited year [S3]. A reader should hold both statements at once: the accounts are prepared on a going-concern basis, and the cash-upstream channel to the parent is closed.

On ESG, the exposures are the ordinary ones for Indonesian animal protein — biosecurity and animal welfare at the cattle and poultry operations, waste and water at slaughter, and the feed supply chain, where imported soybean meal carries a deforestation link — plus two company-specific items. The first is that the group's own foot-and-mouth outbreak remains the reason the debt restructuring began [S3], which makes animal-disease management a live credit risk and not only an operational one. The second is the conditional nature of the current year's reported profit, which is a reporting-quality question we handle in the financial section rather than an environmental one [S3, S4].

Two events carry archivable dates, and we do not manufacture others. The first has happened: the exchange removed WMPP from the special-monitoring board with effect from 28 September 2026, in the same measure that cut the exchange's minimum share price to Rp1.0, naming WMPP among the ninety-two issuers affected [S7, F35, F36]. The second is dated and pending: the exchange's delisting of eighteen issuers takes effect on 10 November 2026, and neither WMPP nor its listed poultry subsidiary is on that list [S6, F37] — a confirmation rather than an event, but one worth tracking because the company's recent history includes a suspension that put the question on the table.

The monitorables are method-specific. First, any return of cash to the parent — a dividend from a subsidiary, a distribution from the parent, a buyback or a stake sale — would attack the discount directly and is the single most honest quality metric for this structure [S0, S3]. Second, the homologated instalment schedule: the balance sheet carries 15.6 IDR bn falling due within a year, and whether the group services it from operations or from asset sales is the credit question [S3]. Third, the parent's carrying value of its stakes: a write-down toward consolidated reality would lower the parts mark, and it is the most likely way the primary valuation moves against us [S3, F6, F19] — and with it the IDR176.0bn of the parent's related-party receivable that sits due from the controlling shareholder's own vehicle, interest-free, unsecured and unprovided, an impairment of which would lower the parts and raise the corporate layer at once [S3, F52]. Fourth, the listed poultry subsidiary's rights issue — up to 6,100,000,000 of new shares, a subscription the parent's own cash of IDR0.2bn cannot fund — which will determine whether the parent's 76.6% interest in the group's best asset is diluted toward a third party [S8, S11, F7, F50, F51]. Fifth, mix: whether the low-margin trading and construction lines keep dominating the top line or whether farming and processing grow into it, which is what would move gross margin off a level barely above zero [S3, S0].

Three named, sourced drivers: the recovery stalls after a first quarter carried by a non-operating gross-up rather than by trading [S4, F32]; the free-meals procurement is reshuffled or delayed, so the company's own expansion plan misses [S2, S8]; and the parts mark proves unsupportable — the controlling shareholder's interest-free, unsecured receivable of IDR 176.0bn is impaired, and the listed poultry arm's rights issue of up to 6.1bn new shares dilutes the parent's 76.6% interest because the parent's own cash is IDR 0.18bn and it cannot fund its share of the subscription [S3, F7, F51, F52]. On this method the target is set by the parts mark and the discount, and the engine holds the parts at the parent's audited book (a fact, not an input the scenario layer can shock), so the bear expresses the parts-write-down risk through the lever the model does carry — a wider discount toward the wide end of the persistent band — and records what would force the parts mark down in reality. The parts-mark sensitivity itself is stated arithmetically in the valuation section rather than implied by the narrative.

bull.narrative: The discount narrows toward the tight end of the persistent band on the things that would actually do it — a return of cash from the subsidiaries to the parent, a stake sale or a subsidiary action that crystallises a mark [S0] — with the free-meals programme's demand delivered into the group's slaughter and processing capacity [S2, F26, F28] and the laying-hen and feedlot expansion arriving on schedule [S8]. This register supports no further MODELABLE bull lever, and we say so rather than dress one up: the listed poultry arm's carrying value is not broken out of the parent's single investment line, so a market re-mark cannot be netted without double-counting [S3, F6], and the PSAK 16 land revaluation surplus is already inside book equity [S3]. Even at the tight end of the band the parts, carried at the parent's own audited book, do not reach the market's price — the bull is capped by the book mark, not by the engine, which is why the bull probability is set below the bear's rather than held at an even split.

sensitivity.title: 12-month value vs holding-company discount and cost of equity

assumptions.label: Revenue growth
assumptions.basis: Taken from what the first quarter of the current year actually shows and held near it, not from the company's plan. Q1 2026 sales were IDR 287.76bn against IDR 204.18bn in Q1 2025, so the witnessed rate is up by roughly two fifths year on year [S4, F30, F31]; annualising that half against FY2025 gives roughly eleven per cent for the full year, which is where FY2026E sits. Management's stated 2026 revenue target of IDR 2.10tn, or +108 per cent — the detik source labels it "kuartal I-2026", but its own comparison base is FY2025's full year (IDR 1.01tn, F3) and a first-quarter reading is impossible on Q1-2026 sales of IDR 0.29tn (F30), so we read it as the annual target (F29) — would need the second half to run at two and a half times the second half of 2025 [S8, F29] and is not a rate we will carry into the base case. The company's own demand case is real and sourced — the free-nutritious-meals programme alone is assumed by the company to absorb 191,210 tonnes of beef in 2026 [S2, F26] — but it is a demand statement, not a revenue number, and we take the witnessed run-rate instead. Growth tapers toward the house macro deck's long-run expansion for Indonesia [S0]: above GDP at first because the group's assets are still far below the volume they can serve, then down to the deck's long-run rate.

assumptions.label: Gross margin at base input costs
assumptions.basis: Set from the witnessed current-year rate rather than the last audited year's, because the last audited year's own margin (IDR 2.79bn of gross profit on IDR 1,011.90bn of sales, [S3, F3]) is the trough of the restructuring and no source supports carrying a trough margin forward. Q1 2026 printed IDR 3.17bn of gross profit on IDR 287.76bn of revenue [S4], an order of magnitude better than the full prior year, and that rate is what the forecast holds flat in real terms. No source supports a further step up either: the segment mix is dominated by low-margin meat and carcass trading [S3, F14], and the group is a price taker in feed, live bird and beef.

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: The last audited year's own operating-expense line over the last audited year's revenue (IDR 103.64bn on IDR 1,011.90bn, [S3]), held flat in real terms. The group has already taken the overhead down through the restructuring and reports a payroll of about five hundred people [S3, F40]; nothing in the register sources a further cut, and a further cut would be an unsourced improvement.

assumptions.label: D&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: Set from the LK's OWN depreciation and amortisation, not the data pack's cash-flow feed: the Note 15 total is IDR 104.92bn for FY2025 and IDR 101.48bn for FY2024 [F1, F2], roughly two and a half times the pack's direct-method figure, which carries no add-back. The ratio of that restated charge to revenue is what the forecast holds.

assumptions.label: Capex / revenue
assumptions.basis: The last audited year's own ratio of capital spending to revenue, held flat. The figure is small (IDR 6.58bn of additions against IDR 1,011.90bn of sales) because the build-out that matters — the poultry complex at WMUU, carried at a little over half complete with a completion target in late 2027 [S3] — was already funded and is being finished with the assets on the balance sheet. We do not raise it (no source states a new programme) and do not cut it (that would be an unsourced improvement in cash flow).

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: The last audited year's own operating working capital over revenue (IDR 650.06bn on IDR 1,011.90bn, [S3, F3]), held flat. The engine's three-year default is higher because it averages in the restructuring years, when revenue collapsed faster than the working-capital base; the last actual's ratio is the one the business is running at now.

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A (div(tax, pbt))

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A (div(interest_expense, debt[-1]))

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A (div(interest_income, cash[-1]))

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: Held at the engine default of no new borrowing, and the report says plainly why rather than fabricating a schedule: the group's debt is the subject of a court-homologated peace agreement that fixes instalments and a deferred interest tail (the balance sheet carries a dedicated "Debt from Homologation Results" line, IDR 15.62bn of it falling due within a year [S3, F23]), and the LK does not state the schedule's undiscounted amounts. On this method the financing path feeds only the small earnings cross-check, not the target.

assumptions.label: Other non-operating items
assumptions.basis: Zero, deliberately, and this is a judgment the report defends: the current year's reported profit comes from other income, not from operations — Q1 2026 booked IDR 1,440.06bn of other income against IDR 1,186.82bn of other expenses and a gross profit of only IDR 3.17bn [S4, F32] — and that gross-up is a restructuring event, not a repeating earnings stream. Carrying any of it into the forecast would put a one-off at the centre of the base case.

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A (div(minority, np))

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: Zero, and sourced rather than assumed by omission. The company has never paid a dividend: the pack's dividend history is empty across every year it covers [S0], no distribution line appears in either the consolidated or the company-only statement of changes in equity [S3], and the parent's unappropriated retained earnings are a deficit at both year-ends [S3, F44] so no distribution is legally possible. A share of profit we cannot source, on a name with a deficit in retained earnings, would be a fabricated leg in the blend; the engine therefore drops the dividend-yield method entirely.

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: This is not a discounted-cash-flow name — the industry's method set is the sum of the parts plus an earnings and a book cross-check, and no perpetual growth rate reaches the target. The input is set at the house's long-run rupiah inflation assumption, inside the house cap for a rupiah reporter, so the cross-check frame is not flattered by a real-growth assumption.

assumptions.label: Holding-company discount to SOTP
assumptions.basis: Anchored on the house base rate — a twenty to forty per cent holdco discount persists indefinitely and narrows only on a named, dated action that actually upstreams cash — and set above the middle of the band, because on this name almost every published fact points the same way [S0]. Against the tight end: the company has never paid a dividend and has a deficit in retained earnings so it cannot [S0, S3, F44]; the parent's own cash is IDR 0.18bn against a company-level liability stack of IDR 1,632.10bn [S3, F7, F10]; there is a large long-term related-party payable at the parent, IDR 194.46bn, and a long-term related-party receivable of similar size, which is the kind of intra-group plumbing that keeps value at the centre rather than pushing it out [S3, F24]; and the shares were suspended by the exchange from the middle of 2024 and only returned to trading in March 2026, having spent that period on the special-monitoring board [S6, S7]. For the tight end: the exit from the special-monitoring board on 28 September 2026 is a real, dated improvement in investability [S7, F35], and the first quarter shows a genuine operating recovery [S4]. We charge thirty-five per cent: off the middle because the cash-upstream channel has never run and the parent has no distributable reserves, short of the wide end because the listing status has been normalised and the businesses are trading again.

challenges.challenge: The report states the free-meals programme "has been the subject of a criminal investigation into its own conduct elsewhere in the country [S2, S8]." Neither cited source says this: S8 (the 22 May 2026 detik expansion note) contains no such sentence, and S2's only occurrence of "investigasi" is the whistleblowing-system boilerplate on S2 line 8203 ("investigasi akan dilakukan dan dijadikan dasar pertimbangan"). A stated external fact about the company's single largest named demand driver, attributed to two sources that do not carry it, is a citation that does not say what the report claims.
challenges.answer: Confirmed as raised: S2 carries no investigation into the meals programme (its only 'investigasi' is the whistleblowing-system boilerplate at S2 line 8203) and S8 carries the word not at all. The sentence and its [S2, S8] citation have been struck from fund record 2. The paragraph now states that the programme is the base case's key demand assumption whose conduct this register gives us no disclosed finding, charge or investigation to cite, and that we assert none; no unsourced claim remains.

challenges.challenge: F29 (revenue_target_2026 = 2,100, unit IDR bn, period FY2026E) is keyed as a full-year target but its own archived quote reads "WMPP menargetkan pendapatan kuartal I-2026 mencapai Rp2,10 triliun" — a Q1-2026 target — and compares it to "periode yang sama tahun lalu sebesar Rp 1,01 triliun", which is FY2025's full-year revenue (1,011.90bn, F3), not Q1-2025 (204.18bn, F31). The source is internally inconsistent, and the "second half must run at two and a half times" argument that rejects the plan is built on this fact. The analyst's FY reading is defensible on the 108.2% arithmetic, but the fact as archived cannot be verified as an annual number.
challenges.answer: F29 has been relabelled to what S8 actually says — a first-quarter-2026 revenue target of Rp2.10trn — and the fact now records in its locator that the source's own period label contradicts its comparison base (S8 compares to Rp1.01trn, which is FY2025's full-year revenue F3, not Q1-2025's F31 of Rp204.18bn). Because a first-quarter reading is arithmetically impossible against F30 (Q1-2026 revenue Rp287.76bn), the reject-the-plan argument in fund record 2 was re-checked and now reconciles F3/F29/F30 explicitly rather than resting on a mislabelled annual figure; the arithmetic (108.2% of FY2025 revenue) is stated as the fact's own basis.

challenges.challenge: The card (VAL_HOLDCO_DISCOUNT §1) requires listed stakes at market value, and this group's poultry business is operated through a separately listed entity, PT Widodo Makmur Unggas Tbk (S3/F42). The report declines to mark it, on the ground that "the register does not carry the listed poultry subsidiary's own price series or the parent's stake percentage in a form this model can consume" — but a listed name has a public price and the parent's interest is a disclosed figure. This is the one part in the whole SOTP that can be marked independently, and it is the largest unaddressed swing factor (a re-rated sub could raise or lower the parts).
challenges.answer: The false rationale has been removed. The listed poultry arm is now disclosed and dated at market: WMUU traded at {{fact.F49|px}} in the third week of October 2026 (S9/F49) and the parent holds {{fact.F50|pctv}} of it (S2/F50) [see fund record 1 and 4]. It is NOT netted into the parts line as a separate component row, and the report now says why rather than hiding behind a missing price series: the parent's balance sheet carries a single 'Investasi Saham' line (F6) that does not break out WMUU's carrying value, so a market re-mark of the stake would double-count an asset already inside F6 by an unsourced amount; and WMUU's listed share count could not be sourced from an archived page (the fetches on market.bisnis.com, id.investing.com and ajaib.co.id returned 403/403/503), so the market cap cannot be struck. The stake is disclosed as the single biggest unaddressed swing factor, which is what the challenge asks for when a full re-mark is not cleanly available.

challenges.challenge: The report presents the bridge as corroboration — "the parts value less the net corporate layer equals the parent's audited equity of 421.49bn exactly ... which is the discipline the card asks for." It is an identity, not a check: fund record defines holdco_net_debt (805.82) as parent total liabilities (1,632.10) less the parent's non-stake assets (826.28), so parts - layer must equal parent equity by construction. The card asks for holdco NET DEBT (debt less cash) plus opex capitalised at ~10x. Using the entire liability stack turns the primary "SOTP" into a book-value P/BV on parent equity (421.49 / 29.419 = 14.33 per share pre-discount), which is a different method from the one the card names.
challenges.answer: The challenge is correct that 'ties exactly' was algebra, not corroboration. fund record valuation.holdco_net_debt_basis now decomposes the layer explicitly: parent total liabilities {{fact.F10}} less non-stake assets (cash {{fact.F7}}, long-term related-party receivable {{fact.F53}}, fixed assets {{fact.F54}}, plus deferred-tax and other balances), netting to 805.82bn, and it states in the same place that the closure to parent equity {{fact.F8}} is an accounting identity and NOT corroboration. The report now presents the layer as a computation and states plainly that the primary is a parent-book net asset value — that is, a P/BV on parent book pre-discount (14.33 a share) — rather than dressing the identity up as an SOTP cross-check. The whole layer is netted rather than only debt-less-cash because the parent's liabilities are mostly related-party payables (e.g. {{fact.F5}}), which we will not treat as remote.

challenges.challenge: The 10% house liquidity charge is stacked on top of the 35% holdco discount (tp construction: blend 10.78 x 1.2124 = 13.07, x (1 - 0.10) = 11.76), and both sit on a parts mark that is itself ~4.8x the consolidated parent-attributable net assets. The holdco-discount band (20-40%, VAL_HOLDCO_DISCOUNT §2) and the liquidity schedule (fund rules 10% below ADTV 2bn) are both pricing illiquidity and the agency of the centre; the base-rate band was struck on liquid large caps. The compound haircut is ~42% of a book value already far above economic reality, and the analyst has no separate calibration showing the two charges measure different things.
challenges.answer: The two charges measure different things and are now stated as such rather than left to look like one factor counted twice. The 35% holdco discount prices the agency of the centre — the controller's discretion over whether value is ever upstreamed to the parent's public shareholders (VAL_HOLDCO_DISCOUNT 2, base rate 20-40%) [S0]. The 10% charge is the house liquidity schedule applied to names trading below the ADTV floor (fund rules ADTV 2bn) [S0]; this name's ADTV is {{mkt.adtv_idr|money}} [S0], so it sits squarely in the schedule. That is written into fund record 4 ('Two charges, two different factors') and into qc_justifications.liquidity.stack. We do not drop either: the discount is the card's default for a structure that has never paid a dividend, and the liquidity charge is a constitutional rule we apply mechanically to every sub-floor name, not a view we are free to waive on this one.

challenges.challenge: The bear narrative says the parent's book value of its stakes "has to be written down toward the consolidated reality", but the bear shocks in fund record move only a.holdco_discount (+0.10) and a.revenue_growth (-0.03). The parts mark — the largest single value lever, and the one the report itself names as "the most likely way the primary valuation moves against us" (7. Catalysts) — is never shocked. Because the primary is discount-driven and revenue does not enter the SOTP, the scenario spread is effectively degenerate (base 13 / bear 12 / bull 14, a +/-1 band), so the bear cannot express its own thesis.
challenges.answer: Accepted, with the model's real constraint stated rather than hidden. The scenario engine can shock only the drivers it holds as inputs — a., d.., m., p.
